why: The PLATE SERIES — eight figures generated at build time from a stated rule, drawn into inline SVG or a pixel buffer, and read from a record where they use one. The operator asked for these by name ("the geometries index").
rule: Mathematics, drawing code and records are crossed byte-for-byte. Every PAGE is rebuilt in this repository’s design system — no bench CSS, no bench HTML, no ECharts. Patches are declared here so they can never be mistaken for drift.
patches: plates.js: the require paths were repointed at THIS repository's records (playground/interferometer/out/, certs/erdos1038-forcing-1.828.json, ./data/) and the bench page-writing tail was replaced by module.exports. The plate FUNCTIONS are untouched — that is the asset.

plates.js PLATE IV: the radius axis ran from 1e-12 to the largest rMax, two decades past the last verified radius, which squeezed every zero crossing — the entire subject — into a hairline. The range is now set by the decisions themselves: a decade below the smallest verified radius, four times above the largest. The vertical range was the same failure and is fixed the same way: symmetric about zero at 1.6x the largest defect, with the clip stated on the plate.

plates.js PLATE VIII: drew all 61 teeth at 14px and 2px a row. The linear programme never reaches past the first handful, so 92% of the picture was black by construction. It now measures how many teeth are ever used, crops to those, gives each row 6px, and states the count in its own footer — 'the programme used three of sixty-one' is the finding, not an excuse for a crop.
